title: thread-scaling: measure serial and parallel time per tool from outside, then shrink the set and run reps
body: The real set is all of Pfam against 500,000 MGnify sequences, sized so that serial work does not dominate any point; one rep, no --reps. A one-off slow single-thread mmseqs run then skewed every efficiency point. The proposal is to measure each tool's serial and parallel time separately, from outside the tools, so the set can shrink a lot and reps become affordable. What survives either stance: a scaling point must not be dominated by fixed costs or by one noisy run, and the fix addresses the cause.
